correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 21–71. Because ℓ divides n−1, the right-hand side is coprime to n; hence gcd(n,φ(n))=1. A repeated prime factor would divide φ(n), and an even composite would share the factor 2 with φ(n); thus only odd squarefree composites need consideration. For n=pq with distinct primes, an independent valuation argument confirms the exclusion: choose a prime r at which p−1 and q−1 have unequal valuations s<t. Then v_r(pq−1)=s, by expanding (p−1)+(q−1)+(p−1)(q−1), whereas v_r(φ(pq))=s+t. Divisibility requires v_r(ℓ)≥t. If s=0 this is impossible because ℓ divides pq−1; if s≥1 it requires valuation at least 2, impossible since ℓ is squarefree. This also confirms the logic of the frozen gcd argument: the coprime quotients a,b must divide ℓ, while gcd(ab,hab+a+b)=1 forces ab to divide h and then the complementary factor of ℓ, contradicting squarefreeness unless p=q. Directly, 1729=7·13·19, φ(1729)=1296, and 3·1728=4·1296 with 3 a squarefree divisor of 1728. The reduced-denominator test d is valid by canceling gcd(φ(n),n−1): admissibility is exactly d squarefree and d|n−1. Read VERIFICATION.md, verify.py and verification_output.txt; the reported finite regression was not rerun and is not needed for the unbounded proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The classical class is narrower. The power-divisibility class is broader: an admissible almost-Lehmer multiplier gives φ(n)|(n−1)^2, while the power family allows examples with extra prime multiplicities. In particular φ(15)=8 divides 14^3 but not any admissible ℓ times 14. The k in that comparison is not an arbitrary coefficient; a solution with a power does give some unrestricted multiplier.

value.rationale: The minimum distinct support is a natural exact invariant of an established Lehmer class. Unlike the known odd squarefree reduction, this result rules out the entire lowest remaining composite support, with a local obstruction showing why the squarefree multiplier constraint excludes two primes even though the adjacent power class admits them. The known example supplies sharpness, not the contribution by itself.
